BURHAN:v3p289/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p289/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BURHAN:v3p289/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj cites “man is ever hasty” as support for understanding haste as the intended sense in “created from haste.”

ITQAN:v4p446/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p446/r2.speaker: المراكشي
ITQAN:v4p446/r2.claim: Al-Marrakushi says omission of waw in these four forms signals an action's speed and ease for its agent and its forceful effect on its object.
ITQAN:v4p446/r2.anchor: قال المراكشي السر في حذفها من هذه الأربعة التنبيه على سرعة وقوع الفعل وسهولته على الفاعل

ITQAN:v4p446/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p446/r3.speaker: المراكشي
ITQAN:v4p446/r3.claim: For وَيَدْعُ الإنسان, omission suggests that a person readily and quickly does evil, perhaps more innately than good.
ITQAN:v4p446/r3.anchor: أما ( ويدع الإنسان ) فيدل على أنه سهل عليه ويسارع فيه كما يسارع في الخير

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Section III invites Jews and Quraysh to the Qur’an's natural straight path, contrasts the fates of acceptance and rejection, rebukes those blind to signs who demand punishment, and alludes to God's practice of punishing nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: both the Jews and the Idolaters of the Quraysh are invited to profess faith in the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verse depicts Qur’an's rivals demanding a punishment sign instead of accepting it; their foolish, destructive demand is described indirectly to express sorrow.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This is a depiction of the rivals of the Qur’ ān who instead of professing faith in it were demanding a sign of punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Rather than using their respite to reform, the rivals make a naïve demand for punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: instead of benefitting from the respite and reforming themselves

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r1.claim: In anger, a person may call on God for evil against himself, family, servants, or property, asking for a curse or destruction.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r1.anchor: ويدعو الله عند غضبه بالشر واللعن والهلاك على نفسه وأهله وخدمه وماله

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r2.claim: The verse attributes a tendency of some people or some moments to the human race generally; the written form omits the final waw in three verbs although its meaning remains.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r2.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس أسند إليه حال بعض أفراده أو حكى عنه حاله

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r3.claim: Calling evil with a prayer like one asks for good would destroy the person if answered; alternatively, people ask for what they think good though it is harmful, so should seek what God deems good rather than what they desire.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r3.anchor: فلو استجيب له إذا دعا باللعن كما يجاب له بالخير لهلك أو يدعوه بما يحسبه خيرا

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r4.claim: People are innately hasty, demanding whatever occurs to them without considering its outcome or waiting for distress to pass.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r4.anchor: يسارع إلى طلب ما يخطر بباله ولا ينظر عاقبته ولا يتأنى

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r5.claim: Kashifi describes people as hastily shifting from one state to another and being unable to endure either adversity or prosperity.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (تعجيل دارد در انقلاب ازحالي بحالي

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r6.claim: A person's hastiness appears in speech and deeds: he persists in acts that cause evil and punishment.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r6.anchor: فالإنسان عجول قولا وفعلا يتمادى في الأعمال الموجبة للشر والعذاب

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r7.claim: A hadith contrasts the believer who pauses with the hypocrite who leaps ahead.

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r8.speaker: آدم
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r8.claim: Adam told his children to pause before acting, saying that a pause would have prevented what happened to him.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r8.anchor: قال آدم عليه السلام لأولاده : كل عمل تريدون أن تعملوا

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r9.speaker: أعرابي
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r9.claim: An Arab warned against haste, calling it the mother of regrets.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r9.anchor: قال أعرابي : إياكم والعجلة فإن العرب تكنيها

BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r10.claim: Haste is condemned except in six cases: timely prayer, burying the dead, marrying a mature virgin, paying due debt, feeding an arriving guest, and repenting promptly.
BURSEVI:v5p104#3/r10.anchor: قيل : العجلة من الشيطان إلا في ستة مواضع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r1.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r1.claim: Shaykh al-Islam says the verse depicts the state of the one guided after describing the guide, showing their contrast.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r1.anchor: بيان الحال المهدي إثر بيان حال الهادي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r2.claim: Al-insān may be generic while describing a disbelieving subset, as Ibn Abbas suggests, or describe anyone at moments such as anger, as reports from al-Hasan and Mujahid suggest.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r2.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس أسند إليه حال بعض أفراده

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r3.claim: The Qurʾān calls people to the greatest good and warns of greatest evil, but disbelievers ask for punishment, as in 8:32 and 11:32.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r3.anchor: أن القرآن يدعو الإنسان إلى الخير الذي لا خير فوقه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r4.claim: The request may be a literal prayer or figuratively sinful deeds leading to punishment; some read utterance as sarcastic haste.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r4.anchor: إما بلسانه حقيقة كدأب من قال منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r5.claim: Duʿāʾahu means his supplication: omitted mithla and comparison particle make it an accusative verbal noun, like his hypothetical prayer for good.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r5.anchor: أي دعائه فحذف الموصوف وحرف التشبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r6.claim: The human in kāna al-insānu ʿajūlan is the same disbelieving person, rashly seeking whatever occurs while blind to harm; the irony is that punishment will come.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r6.anchor: من أسند إليه الدعاء المذكور من أفراده

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r7.claim: If supplication means sinful actions, haste describes persistent deeds making punishment deserved.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r7.anchor: وعلى تقدير حمل الدعاء على أعمالهم تجعل العجولية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r8.claim: Alternatively, anyone under anger abandons prayer for good and invokes harm on self, family, or wealth; humans are innately hasty and irritable.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r8.anchor: أن القرآن يدعو الإنسان إلى ما هو خير وهو في بعض أحيانه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r9.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r9.claim: Al-Waqidi relates from Aisha that a captive escaped while she was distracted; the Prophet angrily said God cut her hand, then explained he was human and prayed any curse on a believer become purification.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r9.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم دخل عليها بأسير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r10.claim: Humans are hasty because they do not deliberate enough to recognize what merits prayer and what deserves protection from.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p23/r10.anchor: وكان الإنسان عجولا غير مستبصر لا يتدبر في أموره حق التدبر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r1.claim: Al-Alusi accepts the first human as the disbeliever: obedience brings favor, disobedience affliction; after praising Qurʾānic guidance, the passage condemns Quraysh for seeking stones or punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r1.anchor: إرادة الكافر من الإنسان الأول بعض المحققين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r2.claim: Al-Kashf connects the verse to Qurʾānic guidance: people refuse its best path and choose the most blameworthy one.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r2.anchor: أن القرآن يهديهم للتي هي أقوم ويأبون إلا التي هي ألوم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r3.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r3.claim: A report from Salman says Adam's head was created first; watching himself form, he urged God to hurry before night while his legs remained unfinished.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r3.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي قال : أول ما خلق الله تعالى من آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r4.claim: Mujahid also transmits a similar story explaining human haste through Adam.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r5.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi, whose attribution al-Alusi treats cautiously, says Adam saw Paradise's fruit when his spirit reached his eyes and rushed toward it once it entered his stomach.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r5.anchor: لما وصلت الروح لعينيه نظر إلى ثمار الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r6.claim: Adam's reading makes haste an inherited trait, but al-Alusi prefers generic humanity; the wording can accommodate Adam despite Abu Hayyan's objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r6.anchor: والأولى إرادة الجنس وإن كان ألفاظ الآية لا تنبو عن إرادة آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r7.claim: The preposition bi in both places is most naturally governed by supplication; readings as in or because of are against the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r7.anchor: الباء في الموضعين على ظاهرها صلة الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r8.speaker: النبي ﷺ
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r8.claim: A report from Jabir says not to pray against oneself, children, or property lest the prayer coincide with an hour when God answers it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r8.anchor: أبو داود والبزار عن جابر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r9.claim: This report rebuts the claim that such prayers are never answered out of divine generosity.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r9.anchor: وبه يرد على ما قيل من أن الدعاء بذلك لا يستجاب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r10.claim: The Prophet's curse-like words to Aisha are explained as correction in anger, with a request that any undeserved invocation become mercy and purification.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r10.anchor: وأجيب عن ذلك بأنه كان للزجر وإن كان وقت الغضب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r11.speaker: النبي ﷺ
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r11.claim: A sound report says the Prophet stipulated that any invocation against a Muslim unworthy of it become purification and nearness to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r11.anchor: قال : إني اشترطت على ربي فقلت إنما أنا بشر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r12.speaker: المازري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r12.claim: Al-Maziri, quoted by al-Nawawi, says the Prophet chose between invocation and another correction; anger for God prompted one lawful option, while unworthiness is judged by God's hidden knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r12.anchor: ما قال المازري من أنه يحتمل أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أراد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r13.claim: Another view treats phrases such as taribat yamīnuk as habitual Arab speech, not intended curses; fearing accidental acceptance, the Prophet asked to turn them into purification, though al-Alusi cautions that reports have problems.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r13.anchor: ليس بمقصود بل هو مما جرت به عادة العرب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r14.claim: Standard grammar would retain the wāw in yadʿu without a jussive, but Qurʾānic form is transmitted as heard and not altered to fit a transmitter's judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p24/r14.anchor: إذ لا جازم تحذف له لكن نقل القرآن العظيم كما سمع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r4.claim: The verse suggests a prayer discipline: seekers should not rush requests but wait to understand what suits their state, since people may ask unknowingly for their own ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r4.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أدب من آداب الدعاء وهو عدم الاستعجال فينبغي للسالك أن يصبر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r5.speaker: سهل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r5.claim: Sahl calls remembrance the safest invocation and recommends leaving choice aside; remembrance suffices, and God gives especially to one whom remembrance distracts from asking.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r5.anchor: وقال سهل : أسلم الدعوات الذكر وترك الاختيار لأن في الذكر الكفاية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r1.claim: The final waw of “calls” is dropped in speech before the still lām and in writing, but remains understood, as in 96:18.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r1.anchor: حذف الواو لفظا لاستقبال اللام الساكنة كقوله: "سندع الزبانية" (العلق-18) ، وحذف في الخط أيضا وهي غير محذوفة في المعنى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r2.claim: In anger, people curse themselves, their children, or property just as they ask for good; if answered they would perish, but God mercifully does not answer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r2.anchor: ومعناه: ويدعو الإنسان على ماله وولده ونفسه، {بالشر} فيقول عند الغضب: اللهم العنه وأهلكه ونحوهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas describes humans as impatient and unable to endure either ease or hardship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p81/r3.anchor: قال جماعة من أهل التفسير وقال ابن عباس: ضجرا لا صبر له على السراء والضراء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r1.claim: When angry, a person may call for evil against self, family, or property, or ask for what seems good but proves evil; such calls resemble calls for good.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r1.anchor: ويدعو الله تعالى عند غضبه بالشر على نفسه وأهله وماله

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r2.claim: People rush toward each thought that occurs to them without considering its consequence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r2.anchor: يسارع إلى كل ما يخطر بباله لا ينظر عاقبته

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r3.claim: One view identifies the human as Adam, who tried to stand before the spirit had reached beyond his navel and fell.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام فإنه لما انتهى الروح إلى سرته

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r4.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet gave a captive to Sawda bint Zam'a; pitying his groans, she loosened his bonds and he escaped. The Prophet prayed that a curse he regretted be made mercy, and the verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r4.anchor: دفع أسيرا إلى سودة بنت زمعة فرحمته لأنينه فأرخت كتافه، فهرب

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r5.claim: Alternatively, the human is an unbeliever who mockingly hastens punishment, like al-Nadr ibn al-Harith's prayer; it was answered and he was executed as a captive at Badr.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:11/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بالإنسان الكافر وبالدعاء استعجاله بالعذاب استهزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r4.claim: A person may invoke harm against himself or loved ones in anger while intending the good; this reveals foolishness, weak judgment, and forgetfulness of what would benefit him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r4.anchor: حذف واوه - الذي هو لام الفعل - خطأ في جميع المصاحف ولا موجب لحذفه لفظا في العربية

BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r5.claim: The written omission of the wāw in yadʿu is not required in pronunciation; the author reads it as signaling foolish desire for harm and an action tending toward ruin until God intervenes, referring to stopping rules in al-Qamar.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r5.anchor: مشير إلى أنه يدعو بالشر لسفهه وقلة عقله , وهو لا يريد علو الشر عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r6.claim: Human beings are innately hasty and rush toward whatever occurs to them without considering its proper moment; they may seek punishment mockingly for themselves or vindictively for others.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r6.anchor: يتسرع إلى طلب كل ما يقع في قلبه ويخطر بباله من غير أن يتأنى فيه تأني المتبصر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r7.claim: ʿAjala means seeking something before its proper time, whereas surʿa means acting at the earliest time that is proper for it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p365/r7.anchor: والعجلة : طلب الشيء في غير وقته الذي لا يجوز تقديمه عليه , وأما السرعة فهي عمله في أول وقته

DURR-FULL:v5p244/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p244/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p244/r13.claim: People hastily pray for harm as they pray for good, saying, for example, “O God, curse him and be angry with him.”
DURR-FULL:v5p244/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير} يعني قول الإنسان

DURR-FULL:v5p246/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r1.claim: Angry people curse children, spouses, themselves, or property; if the curse were granted, it would distress them, so they later ask for good.
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r1.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير} قال: ذلك دعاء الإنسان بالشر على ولده

DURR-FULL:v5p246/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r2.claim: A person hastily curses a child or wife without wanting the harm to occur.
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه: في قوله: {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير} قال: ذلك دعاء الإنسان بالشر على ولده

DURR-FULL:v5p246/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r3.claim: Do not curse yourselves, children, or wealth, since a curse may coincide with an answering hour and be granted.
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r3.anchor: عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا تدعوا على أنفسكم لا تدعوا على أولادكم

DURR-FULL:v5p246/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r4.claim: عجولا means irritable and unable to be patient in prosperity or adversity.
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {وكان الإنسان عجولا} قال: ضجرا لا صبر له على سراء ولا ضراء

DURR-FULL:v5p246/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r5.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r5.claim: Adam watched as his head was created first; with his legs unfinished late in the day, he asked God to hurry before night.
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r5.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي رضي الله عنه قال: أول ما خلق الله من آدم عليه السلام رأسه فجعل ينظر وهو يخلق

DURR-FULL:v5p246/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r6.claim: Adam's eyes were created before the rest of him, and he asked to be completed before sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p246/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: لما خلق الله آدم خلق عينيه قبل بقية جسده فقال: أي رب أتم بقية خلقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.claim: Though the verse’s placement and wording are obscure, the author links it to disbelievers mocking the warning and asking when its promised judgment will arrive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r1.anchor: ولم يأت فيها المفسرون بما ينثلج له الصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.claim: The statement answers the mockery by reminding hearers that the threatened promise has an appointed time; “the human” here means the unbeliever, a common Quranic usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r2.anchor: فالمراد بالإنسان الإنسان الذي لا يؤمن بالآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p41#2/r3.claim: The verb “calls” means seeking or asking for something, as shown by Labid’s poetic usage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r1.claim: The verbal noun compares haste for evil with haste for good: the unbeliever impatiently asks when a threat will come as someone impatiently awaits promised benefit.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r2.claim: The concluding “the human is hasty” generalizes to the human kind, including these unbelievers; kāna marks an established trait, as in another Quranic description.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r2.anchor: فالإنسان هنا مراد به الجنس لأنه المناسب للتذييل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r3.claim: The point is their lack of foresight: God times events wisely and gradually brings both good and evil, rather than granting impatient requests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r3.anchor: الكناية عن عدم تبصره وأن الله أعلم بمقتضى الحكمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r4.claim: The bā’ may reinforce the close link between verb and object, or دعاء may imply hastening, as in “those who do not believe in it hasten it.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r4.anchor: لتأكيد لصوق العامل بمعموله كالتي في قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r5.claim: ʿAjūl is an intensive form of ʿājil, “hasty.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r5.anchor: وعجول : صيغة مبالغة في عاجل . يقال : عجل فهو عاجل وعجول .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r6.claim: The written form omits the wāw in يدع to reflect connected pronunciation; al-Farrā’ says writing it with wāw would also be correct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p42/r6.anchor: قال الفراء : لو كتبت بالواو لكان صوابا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p43/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p43/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p43/r1.claim: The link is that haste cannot alter an appointed term; since terms are spans of time, night and day illustrate their passing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p43/r1.anchor: وهذا شائع عند الناس في أن الزمان متقض وإن طال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r14.claim: The wāw is omitted from yadʿu in the written codex because scribes wrote the recited form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r14.anchor: سقطت الواو من يدع في خط المصحف لأنهم كتبوا المسموع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Mujāhid say the verse rebukes cursing wealth or children in anger; God does not grant rash prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p440#2/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد: هذه الآية نزلت ذامة لما يفعله الناس من الدعاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r1.claim: People inherit haste from Adam, as shown by the verse's wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r1.anchor: فأنتم ذوو عجلة موروثة من أبيكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r2.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r2.claim: Salmān and Ibn ʿAbbās connect haste to Adam, who tried walking before the spirit reached his legs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r2.anchor: إشارته إلى آدم في أنه لما نفخ الروح في رأسه عطس وأبصر فلما مشى الروح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet, bound in Sawda's house, escaped after she loosened his restraint; his prayer against her was mercy because he was human, angry, and hasty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r3.anchor: ويروى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جعل أسيرا في قيد في بيت سودة بنت زمعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r4.claim: One group links the verse to Quraysh's prayer for stones if Muḥammad's message was true; they should instead ask for guidance and mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة هذه الآية نزلت في شأن قريش الذين قالوا اللهم إن كان الحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r5.claim: Another group says people neglect praise in ease but urgently plead for relief in hardship, as in 10:12.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p441/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة: معنى هذه الآية: معاتبة الناس على أنهم إذا نالهم شر

SULAMI:v1p383/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p383/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p383/r1.claim: Sahl says the safest supplication is remembrance while surrendering choice in requests: remembrance suffices, since people may unknowingly ask for their own ruin; the constant rememberer receives the best gifts without the hazards of asking.
SULAMI:v1p383/r1.anchor: قال سهل : أسلم الدعوات الذكر وترك الاختيار في السؤال والدعاء لأن في الذكر الكفاية وربما يدعوا الإنسان

SULAMI:v1p383/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p383/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v1p383/r2.claim: A prophetic report quotes God promising that whoever is occupied by remembrance instead of asking will receive more than those who ask.
SULAMI:v1p383/r2.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' يقول الله عز وجل : من شغله ذكري عن مسألتي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r1.claim: In anger or distress, people pray for harm against themselves and their families as rashly as they pray for good, although they would not want the harmful prayer answered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r1.anchor: يدعو في حال الضجر والغضب على نفسه وأهله بما لا يحب ان يستجاب له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r2.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r2.claim: The human here is generic: the verse refers to people as a class.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r2.anchor: انه اسم جنس يراد به الناس قاله الزجاج وغيره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r3.claim: The human is Adam, whose mention stands for his descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r3.anchor: آدم فاكتفى بذكره من ذكر ولده ذكره ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r4.claim: The human is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who asked for stones to rain from heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r4.anchor: قاله مقاتل وقال سلمان الفارسي أول ما خلق الله من آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r5.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r5.claim: Adam hurried God to finish creating him when only his legs remained; this explains the description of humans as hasty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p13/r5.anchor: قال سلمان الفارسي أول ما خلق الله من آدم رأسه فجعل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r1.claim: People sometimes invoke death, destruction, or a curse against themselves, their children, or property; if God answered, they would perish, as 10:11 says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r1.anchor: {بالشر} أي: بالموت أو الهلاك والدمار واللعنة ونحو ذلك، فلو استجاب له ربه لهلك بدعائه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain the harmful invocation as a person praying for evil against himself or what belongs to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r2.anchor: وكذا فسره ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وقد تقدم في الحديث:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r3.claim: A Prophetic report warns people not to pray against themselves or their property, lest their curse coincide with an hour of divine response.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r3.anchor: "لا تدعوا على أنفسكم ولا على أموالكم، أن توافقوا من الله ساعة إجابة يستجيب فيها"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r4.claim: Human haste and anxiety drive these destructive prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r4.anchor: وإنما يحمل ابن آدم على ذلك عجلته وقلقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r5.speaker: سلمان الفارسي وابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r5.claim: A report from Salman and Ibn Abbas says Adam sneezed and praised God as his soul reached his head; he tried to stand before it reached his legs and asked God to hurry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p49/r5.anchor: فلما وصلت إلى دماغه عطس، فقال: الحمد لله. فقال الله: يرحمك ربك يا آدم.

TUSTARI:17:11/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:17:11/r1.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:17:11/r1.claim: The safest supplication is remembrance and surrendering one’s choices in requests, since a person may unknowingly ask for what will destroy him.
TUSTARI:17:11/r1.anchor: قال سهل: أسلم الدعوات الذكر وترك الاختيار بالسؤال والدعاء، لأن في الذكر الكفاية، وربما يدعو الإنسان ويسأل ما فيه هلاكه

TUSTARI:17:11/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:17:11/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:17:11/r2.claim: Constant remembrance without choosing or asking brings the best desires and frees a person from the harms of requests; God promises the occupied remembrancer more than petitioners receive.
TUSTARI:17:11/r2.anchor: والذاكر على الدوام التارك للاختيار والدعاء والسؤال مبذول له أفضل الرغائب، وساقط عنه آفات السؤال والاختيار،

JISHUMI:v6p4164/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4164/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4164/r1.claim: عجلة means seeking something before its proper time.

JISHUMI:v6p4164/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4164/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4164/r6.claim: The recited form ويدع drops the wāw in pronunciation but not in grammatical meaning, where it remains in the nominative position.
JISHUMI:v6p4164/r6.anchor: وحذف الواو في (ويدع الإنسان) في اللفظ، ولم تحذف في المعنى، لأنها في موضع رفع.

JISHUMI:v6p4166/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والأصم، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r5.claim: The person may curse himself or his children in anger just as he asks God for blessings; if those curses were answered, people would perish, but God mercifully does not answer them.
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r5.anchor: قيل: يدعو على نفسه وولده عند غضبه، فيقول: اللهم العنه واغضب عليه كما يدعو بالخير

JISHUMI:v6p4166/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r6.claim: Another view says a person hastily seeks something harmful to himself, as confirmed by the description of humanity as hasty.
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r6.anchor: وقيل: يطلب ما هو شر له ليتعجل الانتفاع به، يوضحه قوله: وكان الإنسان عجولا وقيل:

JISHUMI:v6p4166/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r7.claim: Abu Muslim compares impatient demands for punishment with eager requests for good and cites examples of people seeking punishment before mercy.
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r7.anchor: عن أبي مسلم، يبين الله تعالى أن تدبيره لأنفسهم خير من تدبيرهم لأنفسهم

JISHUMI:v6p4166/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r8.speaker: مجاهد، وقتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r8.claim: Mujahid and Qatada gloss humanity's haste as praying for harm to arrive quickly, even when it would be unwelcome.
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r8.anchor: وكان الإنسان عجولا قيل: عجولا بالدعاء على ما يكره أن يستجاب له فيه، عن مجاهد، وقتادة، وقيل:

JISHUMI:v6p4166/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r9.claim: Another gloss describes people as impatient and unable to endure hardship and distress.
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r9.anchor: وقيل: ضجرا لا صبر له على البأساء والضراء، وقيل:

JISHUMI:v6p4166/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r10.claim: A story attributed to Ibn Abbas says Adam tried to rise when the soul had reached his feet but not yet his whole body; the author rejects it because an incomplete body cannot intend or act.
JISHUMI:v6p4166/r10.anchor: وقيل: آدم لما نفخ فيه الروح فبلغت إلى رجليه قبل أن تجري فيهما رام النهوض، حكي ذلك عن ابن عباس، وهذا لا يصح لأنه ما لم تصر الجملة حية لا يصح منها الإرادة ولا الفعل

AKHFASH:v2p421/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p421/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p421/r4.claim: دعاءه is an accusative verbal noun governed by the verb, like انك منطلق انطلاقا.
AKHFASH:v2p421/r4.anchor: وقال {دعاءه بالخير} فنصب "الدعاء" على الفعل كما تقول: "إنك منطلق انطلاقا".

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r1.claim: In anger a person invokes evil on himself, family, or possessions just as he invokes good for them, as in the verse about people hastening for evil.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r1.anchor: ويدعو الله عند غضبه بالشر على نفسه وأهله وماله ، كما يدعوه لهم بالخير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r2.claim: People are hasty, asking immediately for whatever enters their thoughts without reflective deliberation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r2.anchor: يتسرع إلى طلب كل ما يقع في قلبه ويخطر بباله ، لا يتأنى فيه تأني المتبصر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r3.claim: A captive escaped after Sawda loosened his bonds; when the Prophet angrily prayed that her hands be cut, she raised them expecting it, and he explained that his imprecations on undeserving family are meant as mercy because he is human and becomes angry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r3.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إني سألت الله أن يجعل لعنتي ودعائي على من لا يستحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r4.claim: Alternatively, the human is an unbeliever who mocks by demanding punishment when hardship strikes, just as he asks for good; since punishment is certain, there is no reason to hasten it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد بالإنسان الكافر ، وأنه يدعو بالعذاب استهزاء ويستعجل به ، كما يدعو بالخير إذا مسته الشدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the person as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who demanded punishment if the message were true and was then executed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p609/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هو النضر بن الحرث قال : اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك الآية

FARRA:v2p117/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p117/r1.claim: The final wāw in ويدع is absent in pronunciation but remains in grammatical sense; it is omitted before the following silent lām, as in related forms.
FARRA:v2p117/r1.anchor: حذفت الواو منها في اللفظ ولم تحذف في المعنى لأنها في موضع رفع

FARRA:v2p117/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p117/r2.claim: Poetry shows a final wāw omitted before the following consonant in كفاك كف ما تليق درهما.
FARRA:v2p117/r2.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
كفاك كف ما تليق درهما ... جودا وأخرى تعط بالسيف الدما

FARRA:v2p117/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p117/r3.claim: A verse by one of the Anṣār likewise has تخف for تخفي.
FARRA:v2p117/r3.anchor:
وقال بعض الأنصار:
ليس تخفى بشارتي قدر يوم ... ولقد تخف شيمتي إعساري

FARRA:v2p117/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p117/r4.claim: People invoke evil as they invoke good, for example praying against a child; God’s not answering such an evil request is itself a favor.
FARRA:v2p117/r4.anchor: يريد كدعائه بالخير في الرغبة إلى الله عز وجل فيما لا يحب الداعي إجابته

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r1.claim: One explanation is that a person seeks immediate benefit through harm that will return to hurt him in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r1.anchor: أن يطلب النفع في العاجل بالضر العائد عليه في الآجل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r2.claim: Another explanation is that people curse themselves or their children with death; if such a curse were answered like a good prayer, they would perish.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r2.anchor: أحدهم على نفسه أو ولده بالهلاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r3.claim: Human haste refers to people hastily praying against themselves, their children, or what concerns them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r3.anchor: وما يخصه , وهذا قول ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r4.speaker: إبراهيم والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r4.claim: Alternatively, the verse refers to Adam, who hurried to rise when the spirit had reached his navel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p232/r4.anchor: حتى بلغت إلى سرته فأراد أن ينهض عجلا , وهذا قول إبراهيم والضحاك

MUQATIL:17:9-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:9-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:9-11/r3.claim: The person praying for evil against himself is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who demanded punishment in 8:32, just as people pray for good for themselves.

MUQATIL:17:9-11/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:9-11/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:9-11/r4.claim: Human haste is illustrated by Adam trying to sit when the spirit had reached only his middle, before reaching his feet; al-Nadr similarly hastened his self-directed curse, and humanity inherited haste from Adam.
MUQATIL:17:9-11/r4.anchor: يعني آدم، عليه السلام، حين نفخ فيه الروح من قبل رأسه، فلما بلغت الروح وسطه عجل، فأراد أن يجلس

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r1.claim: People pray for harm against themselves, servants, or property, asking for what would destroy them if granted.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r1.anchor: {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير} أي يدعو على نفسه وعلى خادمه وعلى ماله، بما لو استجيب له فيه، هلك.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r2.claim: Human beings hurry to pray when angry, while God does not hasten to answer.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p251#7/r2.anchor: {وكان الإنسان عجولا} أي يعجل عند الغضب. والله لا يعجل بإجابته.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r1.claim: A person in anger may call for evil against himself, family, property, or children just as he asks good for them; alternatively, he hastily seeks small immediate benefit even at the cost of greater future harm.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r1.anchor: يدعو الله عند غضبه بالشر على نفسه وأهله وماله وولده كما يدعو لهم بالخير

NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r2.claim: Humans are hasty, pursuing whatever enters their minds without the deliberation of a reflective person.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r2.anchor: يتسرع إلى طلب كل ما يقع في قلبه ويخطر بباله لا يأتى فيه تأنى المتبصر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, “the human” means the disbeliever, who mockingly asks for punishment and hastens it as he would ask good when distressed; punishment is certain, so such haste is pointless.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r3.anchor: أو اريد بالإنسان الكافر وأنه يدعوه بالعذاب استهزاء ويستعجل به

NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the person who invoked punishment as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who challenged that if the message were true God should send the punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هو النصر بن الحرث قال اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r5.claim: In the written text, the wāw is omitted from yadʿu to match its spoken form.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p280#3/r5.anchor: وسقوط الواو من يدع في الخط على موافقة اللفظ

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r1.claim: People in distress sometimes call evil against themselves or their children, just as they would pray for good; God’s mercy keeps such prayers from being answered.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: هو دعاء الرجل على نفسه وولده عند الضجر بما لا يحب أن يستجاب له

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r2.claim: One view says the verse was revealed about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who asked for stones from heaven or painful punishment if Muhammad’s message were true.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r2.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في النضر بن الحارث، كان يدعو ويقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r3.claim: Another view is that people seek forbidden things as eagerly as permitted ones; Ibn Jamiʿ’s poem depicts a worshipper hoping to obtain a woman who carries a camel litter.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو أن يدعو في طلب المحظور كما يدعو في طلب المباح، قال الشاعر وهو ابن جامع:

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r4.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r4.claim: Al-Jawhari explains maḥmil as a support or object of reliance, one of the camel litters, or a sword’s strap.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r4.anchor: قال الجوهري: يقال ما على فلان محمل مثال مجلس أي معتمد.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r5.claim: The written and spoken form drops the wāw of يَدْعُ, although it remains grammatically understood, as in other Qur’anic forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r5.anchor: وحذفت الواو من «ويدع الإنسان» في اللفظ والخط ولم تحذف في المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r6.claim: Human beings are hasty by nature and rush to ask for harm as they rush to ask for good.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r6.anchor: أي طبعه العجلة، فيعجل بسؤال الشر كما يعجل بسؤال الخير.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r7.speaker: سلمان
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r7.claim: Salman says Adam asked to be hurried when his legs had not yet received the spirit, explaining human haste.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r7.anchor: قال سلمان: أول ما خلق الله تعالى من آدم رأسه فجعل ينظر وهو يخلق جسده

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam tried to rise when the spirit reached his navel but could not yet do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما انتهت النفخة إلى سرته نظر إلى جسده فذهب لينهض

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud says Adam rushed toward Paradise’s fruit when he saw it and craved food before the spirit reached his legs, echoing the statement that humans were created hasty.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11/r9.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: لما دخل الروح في عينيه نظر إلى ثمار الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r1.claim: A report in Sahih Muslim says Satan circled Adam after he was formed and recognized that, being hollow, he would not restrain himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r1.anchor: لما صور الله تعالى آدم في الجنة تركه ما شاء الله أن يتركه فجعل إبليس يطيف به

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r2.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r2.claim: Al-Qushayri says the verse followed the Prophet’s curse on an escaped prisoner; the Prophet explained that an undeserved curse from his human anger was a mercy for his family.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r2.anchor: ونزلت الآية ذكره القشيري أبو نصر رحمه الله

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r3.claim: In Sahih Muslim the Prophet asks God to make any harm, insult, or beating he inflicted on a believer an expiation and a means of nearness; similar reports come from Aisha and Jabir.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r3.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that people choose immediate gain, however small, over the lasting reward, however great.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:11#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: معنى «وكان الإنسان عجولا» أي يؤثر العاجل وإن قل، على الآجل وإن جل.

RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r1.claim: The verse’s coherence is that people may turn away from the Qur’an’s laws and explanations despite receiving this great divine gift, and pursue what brings no benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r1.anchor: بعد أن أنزل الله عليه القرآن وخصه بهذه النعمة العظيمة والكرامة الكاملة ، قد يعدل عن التمسك

RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r2.claim: One view identifies the person calling for evil as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who invoked God to bring the claimed truth and was answered by execution; others demanded punishment or asked when the threat would come.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r2.anchor: القول الأول : المراد منه : النضر بن الحرث حيث قال : { اللهم إن كان هاذا هو الحق

RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r3.claim: Another view says angry people curse themselves, family, children, and property; if evil prayers were granted as readily as good ones, they would perish.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r3.anchor: المراد أنه في وقت الضجر يلعن نفسه وأهله وولده وماله

RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed that Sawda’s hand be cut after she loosened a captive’s restraints, then explained that an undeserved angry prayer against family becomes mercy; he told her to lower her raised hand.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r4.anchor: فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( اللهم اقطع يدها ) فرفعت سودة يدها تتوقع

RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r5.claim: Razi proposes that people may eagerly ask for what they think good although it is harmful, because haste and surface appearances keep them from investigating its reality.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد : أن الإنسان قد يبالغ في الدعاء طلبا لشيء يعتقد أن خيره فيه

RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r6.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the written muṣḥaf omits the expected wāw in yadʿu because it is not pronounced; it remains understood grammatically, like other omitted letters, and spelling it would also be correct.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r6.anchor: البحث الرابع : القياس : إثبات الواو في قوله : { ويدع } إلا أنه حذف في المصحف

RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r7.claim: The omission of a few letters in the written text while others remain proves the Qur’an was preserved as heard, with no human editorial changes.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130/r7.anchor: فإن إثبات الياء والواو في أكثر ألفاظ القرآن وعدم إثباتهما في هذه المواضع المعدودة يدل

RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r1.claim: One view says “the human” means Adam: when the spirit reached his navel, he admired his body and tried to rise before he could, showing haste.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r1.anchor: القول الأول : آدم عليه السلام ، وذلك لأنه لما انتهت الروح إلى سرته

RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r2.claim: The other view takes “the human” generically: everyone is prone to haste, though abandoning it would improve religion and worldly life; Razi says this is the underlying point even if Adam is intended.
RAZI-FULL:v20p130#2/r2.anchor: والقول الثاني : أنه محمول على الجنس ، لأن أحدا من الناس لا يعرى عن عجلة

NAHHAS:v2p417/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p417/r7.claim: The weak final wāw in ويدع is omitted in connected recitation after meeting a quiescent letter; outside Qurʾanic orthography it must be restored at pause.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r7.anchor: حذفت الواو في الإدراج لالتقاء الساكنين ولا ينبغي أن يوقف عليه لأنه في السواد بغير واو

NAHHAS:v2p417/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p417/r8.claim: The singular verb’s root wāw is not deleted except in jussive form or liaison; the same applies to يدعو and يرجو.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r8.anchor: لم يجز أن يقف إلا بالواو لأنها لام الفعل لا تحذف إلا في الجزم أو في الادراج

NAHHAS:v2p417/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p417/r9.claim: The alif after plural wāw distinguishes it from the singular verb’s root wāw.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r9.anchor: وإنما تكون الألف مع واو الجميع فرقا بينها وبين الواو التي تكون لام الفعل في الواحد

NAHHAS:v2p417/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r10.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p417/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash says that alif distinguishes the plural marker from conjunction wāw.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r10.anchor: وقال الأخفش : تكون في الجميع فرقابينها وبين واو العطف

NAHHAS:v2p417/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r11.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
NAHHAS:v2p417/r11.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya says the alif distinguishes a detached object pronoun from an emphatic pronoun.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r11.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى : تكون فرقا بين المضمر المنصوب والمؤكد

NAHHAS:v2p417/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r12.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p417/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash takes دعاءه بالخير as an ordinary verbal noun, like انطلقت انطلاقا.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r12.anchor: ^ ( دعاءه بالخير ) ^ قال الأخفش : هذا كما تقول : انطلقت انطلاقا ، أي هو مصدر

NAHHAS:v2p417/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r13.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p417/r13.claim: Al-Farraʾ understands دعاءه بالخير as meaning like his invocation.

NAHHAS:v2p417/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p417/r14.claim: Abu Jaʿfar rejects ellipsis of kāf as affecting case: with kāf, عمرو كالأسد, and without it, عمرو الأسد; the sense is an invocation like his invocation for good.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r14.anchor: قال أبو جعفر : وليس حذف الكاف مما يوجب نصبا ولا غيره ولا اختلاف بين النحويين أنه يقال : عمرو كالأسد

NAHHAS:v2p417/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p417/r15.claim: The full meaning is that a person asks for evil with an invocation like his invocation for good, with the adjective and genitive complement standing for their nouns.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r15.anchor: وحقيقة القول في الآية أن التقدير يدعو الانسان بالشر دعاءا مثل دعائه بالخير ثم أقيمت الصفة مقام الموصوف

STUDYQURAN:17:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r1.claim: People may ignorantly pray for what seems beneficial but will actually harm them, or in anger curse themselves, family, or property; answering such prayers would destroy humanity.
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r1.anchor: people pray in ignorance for what seems beneficial to them but will only bring them harm

STUDYQURAN:17:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r2.claim: Human haste appears in rushing toward disbelief, sin, and enmity, seeking evil before good, and demanding warned-of punishments; 21:37 calls haste intrinsic to humanity.
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r2.anchor: people hasten unto disbelief (5:41) and to sin and enmity (5:62)

STUDYQURAN:17:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r3.speaker: a report
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r3.claim: A report says Adam impatiently tried to stand before the Spirit had reached his feet as life entered his body from his head downward.
STUDYQURAN:17:11/r3.anchor: when God breathed His Spirit into Adam, He started from the head, and as the Spirit flowed downward

TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r1.claim: In anger or distress, people call for evil on themselves, children, and property just as they ask God for health and safety; God mercifully does not grant the harmful requests.
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r1.anchor: العافية، ويرزقه السلامة في نفسه وماله وولده، يقول: فلو استجيب له في دعائه على نفسه وماله وولده بالشر كما يستجاب له في الخير هلك،

TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says people ask God to curse or become angry with someone; if such prayers were answered as quickly as prayers for good, the person would perish.
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا} [الإسراء: 11] يعني قول الإنسان: اللهم العنه

TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates the verse to 10:12 and says remembering and obeying God in good times, as one calls on Him in hardship, would be better.
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r3.anchor: قال: ويقال: هو {وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما} [يونس: 12] أن يكشف ما به من ضر،

TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says people curse their property and children; if God granted those wishes, He would destroy them.
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا} [الإسراء: 11] يدعو على ماله،

TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r5.claim: In another report Qatāda says people pray for harm to themselves, servants, or property that would destroy them if granted.
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير} [الإسراء: 11] قال: يدعو على نفسه بما لو استجيب له هلك،

TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid says people hastily pray for harm to a spouse or child although they do not want the harm to happen.
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا} [الإسراء: 11] قال: ذلك دعاء الإنسان بالشر

TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid and the preceding interpreters take human hastiness to mean rashly asking for disliked things to be granted; another view attributes the trait to Adam's haste to rise before his creation was complete.
TAB-FULL:v14p512#2/r7.anchor: واختلف في تأويل قوله: {وكان الإنسان عجولا} [الإسراء: 11] فقال مجاهد ومن ذكرت قوله:

TAB-FULL:v14p514/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p514/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
TAB-FULL:v14p514/r1.claim: Salman al-Fārisi recounts that Adam watched as he was created from the head downward and asked God to hurry before night, explaining human haste.
TAB-FULL:v14p514/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم، أن سلمان الفارسي، قال: أول ما خلق الله من آدم رأسه، فجعل ينظر وهو يخلق،

TAB-FULL:v14p514/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p514/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p514/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that as the spirit entered Adam from his head, his body became flesh and blood; when it reached his navel he admired his form and tried to rise, showing impatience in ease and hardship.
TAB-FULL:v14p514/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال: لما نفخ الله في آدم من روحه أتت النفخة من قبل رأسه،

TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r1.claim: Duʿāʾ means any request, verbal or enacted through pursuit, since God alone truly gives and withholds; seeking is a request of God whether one realizes it or not.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r1.anchor: المراد بالدعاء على ما يستفاد من السياق مطلق الطلب سواء كان بلفظ الدعاء

TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r2.claim: Human haste means pursuing desire without pausing to consider benefit or harm, so one may rush toward something harmful or beneficial.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#2/r2.anchor: لا يأخذ بالأناة إذا أراد شيئا حتى يتروى ويتفكر في جهات صلاحه وفساده

TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r1.claim: The context admonishes humanity’s haste, which keeps people from valuing guidance and leads them to seek misery as impulsively as happiness.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r1.anchor: فهو سبحانه يلوم الإنسان أنه لما به من قريحة الاستعجال لا يقدر نعمة الهداية

TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r2.claim: “The human” means humankind generally, not only disbelievers; duʿāʾ is unrestricted seeking, and good and evil mean true felicity or misery rather than any benefit or harm.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r2.anchor: أن المراد بالإنسان هو الجنس دون أفراد معينة منه كالكفار والمشركين

TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r3.claim: Haste is wanting a desire to become real immediately, not persistence in asking for punishment; other exegetes’ tangled readings are omitted as unhelpful.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#3/r3.anchor: وبالعجلة حب الإنسان أن يسرع ما يهواه إلى التحقق

TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.claim: The surrounding rebuke links human haste to the record of deeds: people fail to distinguish benefit from harm and rush after desires, though every deed remains with its doer and will be reviewed.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.anchor: أنزل القرآن وجعله هاديا إلى ملة هي أقوم جريا على السنة الإلهية في هداية الناس

TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.claim: The author omits reports on these verses transmitted through both Sunni and Shiʿi routes from the Prophet, Ali, Salman, and others because they lack Quranic, prophetic, or decisive rational support and have weak chains.
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.anchor: روايات تركنا إيرادها لعدم تأيدها بكتاب أو سنة أو حجة عقلية قاطعة مع ما فيها من ضعف الأسناد

TABRISI:17:9-11/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:9-11/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:9-11/r2.claim: The muṣḥaf omits the wāw in يدع although it is present in meaning.
TABRISI:17:9-11/r2.anchor: ولا يكتب الواو في يدع في المصحف

TABRISI:17:9-11/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:9-11/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
TABRISI:17:9-11/r10.claim: People may curse themselves, family, or property in anger as they ask for good; mercy prevents God from granting that destructive request.
TABRISI:17:9-11/r10.anchor: على نفسه وأهله وماله بما لا يحب أن يستجاب له

TABRISI:17:9-11/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:9-11/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:9-11/r11.claim: Other views say people may seek evil in haste for benefit or pursue forbidden things as eagerly as permitted ones.

TABRISI:17:9-11/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:9-11/r12.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:17:9-11/r12.claim: People are hasty because they ask for evil as quickly as good.
TABRISI:17:9-11/r12.anchor: يعجل بالدعاء في الشر عجلته بالدعاء في الخير عن مجاهد

TABRISI:17:9-11/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:9-11/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:9-11/r13.claim: Another meaning is impatience and inability to bear hardship or ease.
TABRISI:17:9-11/r13.anchor: ضجرا لا صبرا له على ضراء ولا على سراء عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:17:9-11/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:9-11/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:9-11/r14.claim: A report applies haste to Adam: when the spirit reached his navel he tried to rise before able, and humanity shares his haste for things before their time.
TABRISI:17:9-11/r14.anchor: أراد به آدم ع لما انتهت النفخة إلى سرته

TABRISI:17:12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:12/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:12/r9.claim: After warning of punishment, the passage says people ignorantly rush to request it; God responds with what benefits them and grants night and day despite their ingratitude.
TABRISI:17:12/r9.anchor: مما تقدم من بشارة الكفار بالعذاب

THALABI:v6p86#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p86#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p86#2/r4.claim: The final wāw of “yadʿu” is omitted in speech and writing but implied grammatically, for ease before a still lām; the author cites several parallel deletions.
THALABI:v6p86#2/r4.anchor: ويدع الإنسان حذفت الواو هنا في اللفظ والخط ولم يحذف في المعنى

THALABI:v6p86#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p86#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p86#2/r5.claim: In anger people invoke harm against their wealth, children, and selves just as they ask for blessings; God mercifully does not hasten to answer harmful wishes.
THALABI:v6p86#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية ويدع الإنسان على [ماله وولده ونفسه بالسوء]

THALABI:v6p86#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p86#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p86#2/r6.claim: Such rash curses include “God curse him” or “destroy it”; they are the harmful counterpart of asking for health and safety.
THALABI:v6p86#2/r6.anchor: والغضب: اللهم العنه اللهم أهلكه دعاءه بالخير أي كدعائه ربه أن يهب له العافية

THALABI:v6p86#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p86#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p86#2/r7.claim: God’s restraint parallels the verse saying that if He hastened evil as people hasten good, their term would be ended; humans are hasty in asking for what they dislike.
THALABI:v6p86#2/r7.anchor: نظيره قوله تعالى ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم

THALABI:v6p86#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p86#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p86#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid and other commentators say the human is hasty; Ibn ʿAbbās says he is impatient and lacks endurance in ease or hardship.
THALABI:v6p86#2/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين، وقال ابن عباس: [يريد] ضجرا لا صبرا له

THALABI:v6p87/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p87/r1.speaker: قوم من المفسرين
THALABI:v6p87/r1.claim: Some commentators identify the human in the verse specifically as Adam.
THALABI:v6p87/r1.anchor: وقال قوم من المفسرين: أراد الإنسان آدم.

THALABI:v6p87/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p87/r2.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
THALABI:v6p87/r2.claim: Salman al-Fārisī says Adam’s head was created first; seeing his body take shape, he asked God to hurry before night while his legs were not yet animated.
THALABI:v6p87/r2.anchor: قال سلمان الفارسي: أول ما خلق الله من آدم رأسه، فجعل ينظر وهو يخلق جسده

THALABI:v6p87/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p87/r3.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p87/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that Adam admired his formed body and tried to rise before he could, illustrating haste.
THALABI:v6p87/r3.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: لما خلق الله رأس آدم نظر إلى جسده فأعجبه

THALABI:v6p87/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p87/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p87/r4.claim: Another report says a captive escaped after Sawda released him; the Prophet regretted praying against her and asked that any such prayer become mercy, after which this verse was revealed.
THALABI:v6p87/r4.anchor: فدعا النبي عليها بقطع اليد ثم ندم فقال: اللهم إنما أنا بشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the written form drops the final wāw of yadʿū although it remains grammatically present; he compares 50:41 and 54:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r1.anchor: القياس إثبات الواو في ويدعو، وحذف في المصحف من الكتابة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r2.claim: In anger or impatience, people may pray for harm on themselves, family, or children just as they pray for good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r2.anchor: أن الإنسان ربما دعا عند الضجر والغضب على نفسه وأهله وولده بما لا يحب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r3.claim: The generic human being rushes to invoke what harms him as quickly as he asks for good; this is the commentators' common explanation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r4.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, the human is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who made the challenge quoted in 8:32; the good prayer is the believers' request for mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {ويدع الإنسان} يعني النضر بن الحارث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains the human's haste as Adam trying to rise before the spirit had fully entered his body.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p270/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء

SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r1.claim: The ordinary sense attaches both باء prepositions to الدعاء: in distress a person may pray for evil and press for it as he does for good.
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنهما متعلقتان بالدعاء على بابهما نحو: " دعوت بكذا "

SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r2.claim: Taking both prepositions as في means that in adversity people urgently pray for relief as they pray in prosperity; what they ask for is neither evil nor good, a reading the author calls remote.
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنهما بمعنى " في " بمعنى أن الإنسان إذا أصابه ضر

SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa takes the prepositions as causal, but the author says the meaning does not support that reading.
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r3.anchor: الثالث: أن تكون للسبب، ذكره أبو البقاء، والمعنى لا يساعده

SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r4.claim: دعاءه is a verbal noun annexed to its agent.
SAMIN-DURR:17:11/r4.anchor: والمعنى لا يساعده، والمصدر مضاف لفاعله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r1.claim: In anger or distress, people may pray against themselves, children, or family in ways they would not want answered, just as they pray for good.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r1.anchor: ربما يدعو الإنسان على نفسه عند الغضب والضجر، وعلى ولده وأهله بما لا يحب أن يستجاب له

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r2.claim: People hasten to pray for evil as quickly as they hasten to pray for good.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:11/r2.anchor: يعجل في الدعاء بالشر كعجلته في الدعاء بالخير.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119/r7.claim: People call for harm against themselves, children, or property just as they call for good; if God hastened the harm people request as in 10:11, those prayed against would die.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119/r7.anchor: قوله: {ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير} [الإسراء: 11] يدعو بالشر على نفسه وعلى ولده وماله كما يدعو بالخير.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r1.claim: The human being’s haste was explained earlier in the commentary.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r1.anchor: {وكان الإنسان عجولا} [الإسراء: 11] وقد فسرناه قبل هذا الموضع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says people curse their property and children; if the curse were answered, they would be destroyed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r2.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: يدعو على ماله فيلعن ماله وولده، ولو استجاب الله له لأهلكه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r3.speaker: حميد بن هلال
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r3.claim: Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl condemns people’s heedlessness of God’s majesty: they curse a mount or sheep, though they would resent being told to curse their own animal.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p119#2/r3.anchor: الحسن بن دينار، عن حميد بن هلال، قال: ألا تعجب من الناس كيف يغبنون عن جلال الله؟

ELMALILI:17:11/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:11/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:11/r1.claim: Humans call for evil as if praying for good: they may ask for punishment as though it were reward, or invite it through their actions.
ELMALILI:17:11/r1.anchor: insan, hayra dua eder gibi şerre dua veya şerri davet eder.

ELMALILI:17:11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:11/r2.claim: Impatience makes people demand the future before its time; instead of patiently seeking reward through faith and good works, they wish painful punishment on unbelievers to arrive immediately.
ELMALILI:17:11/r2.anchor: İnsan acûldür pek acelecidir. Sonra olacak şeyi vaktinden evvel oluversin ister.

ELMALILI:17:11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:11/r3.claim: Because premature demands can end in deprivation, believers should avoid praying for evil, patiently ask for good, and actively pursue it through righteous deeds.
ELMALILI:17:11/r3.anchor: mü’minler şerre dua etmemeli, sabr u teennî ile hayra dua etmeli

ELMALILI:17:11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:11/r4.claim: Human haste also means preferring immediate worldly gain to deferred afterlife reward; Elmalılı says the next passage on seeking the immediate life clarifies this, while qualifying the trait as characteristic of the species or some states, not every person or circumstance.
ELMALILI:17:11/r4.anchor: İnsan peşincidir. Veresiyeden ziyade peşine heves eder, âhireti dünyada görmek ister.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r1.speaker: tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r1.claim: Some polytheists expressed defiance by asking God to rain stones on them if the Quran was truly from Him; the commentary says they are probably meant here.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r2.claim: Some people in distress curse themselves and wish for death instead of patiently seeking reasonable and lawful relief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r2.anchor: şeklindeki sözlerle kendilerine beddua edenler de bulunur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r3.claim: Through ignorance, people may ask for what seems good but is actually harmful, since what people judge good or bad can be the reverse; God knows best.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r3.anchor: insanlar bilgisizlikleri sebebiyle kendi iyiliklerine zannederek aslında yine kendileri için kötü olan şeyleri isterler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r4.claim: Human haste is a weakness: people should use reason, knowledge, experience, or trusted sources to judge, while immature people driven by desire often rush into wrong choices; the verse points them to Quranic standards.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:11/r4.anchor: insanın tabiatındaki bir zaafa işaret etmektedir. Gerçekten insanın, özellikle ilk defa karşılaştığı durumlarda neyin iyi neyin kötü

ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r1.claim: People may angrily pray for evil against themselves, children, or family just as they pray for good; this is a human-wide trait, and al-insān here means people.
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r1.anchor: أن الإنسان ربما دعا على نفسه وولده وأهله

ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r2.claim: A report tells how Sawda bint Zamʿa loosened a prisoner’s shackles after he complained, he escaped, and the Prophet prayed against her in anger; he explained that unjust curses from him are mercy for the undeserving and told her he is human and can become angry.
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r2.anchor: ويروى أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - رفع إلى سودة

ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r3.claim: God’s statement that humanity was created hasty applies to all people, from Adam through the last of his descendants.
ZAJJAJ:v3p229/r3.anchor: فأعلم الله - عز وجل - أن الإنسان خلق عجولا

ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n11/r1.claim: In this context, Asad takes the conjunction wa to mean 'as it is.'
ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n11/r1.anchor: This, to my mind, is the meaning of the conjunctive particle wa in the above context

ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n12/r1.claim: The contrast in 2:216 shows that divine guidance is the only objective criterion of good and bad.
ASAD-NOTES:17:11#n12/r1.anchor: in other words, divine guidance is the only objective criterion as to what is good and what is bad

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#3/r1.claim: People sometimes call for harm to themselves, servants, or property just as they call for good, and the harmful prayer may destroy them if answered.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#3/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعاءه بالخير ﴾ قال يدعو على نفسه بما استجيب له هلك أو على خادمه أو على ماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r7.claim: They say the verse condemns people who pray against their property and children in anger or distress.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r7.anchor: ويدع الإنسان قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة: نزلت ذامة لما يفعله الناس من الدعاء على أموالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r8.claim: The context includes deniers who call for the afterlife’s promised evil to be hastened, as al-Naḍr did.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p18/r8.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أن بعض من لا يؤمن بالآخرة كان يدعو على نفسه بتعجيل ما وعد به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r1.claim: The spelling ويدع omits wāw according to pronunciation; الإنسان is generic for the impatient person who calls harm on self, family, or wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r1.anchor: وكتب ويدع بغير واو على حسب السمع والإنسان هنا ليس واحدا معينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r2.speaker: سلمان الفارسي، ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r2.claim: They connect haste to Adam’s impatience as the spirit entered his body; Abū Ḥayyān says the wording does not fit this account.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r2.anchor: وعن سلمان الفارسي وابن عباس: أشار به إلى آدم لما نفخ الروح في رأسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r3.claim: Another view condemns Quraysh for demanding stones if Muḥammad’s message was true; they should have asked for guidance and mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هذه الآية ذم لقريش الذين قالوا: اللهم إن كان هذا هو الحق من عندك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r4.claim: Another view reproaches people who urgently seek relief in hardship rather than praying as earnestly in prosperity; bāʾ then means “in.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هي معاتبة للناس على أنهم إذا نالهم شر وضر دعوا وألحوا في الدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says that reading conflicts with دعاءه, which implies an actual good-time prayer, not merely one that ought to exist.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r5.anchor: وينبو عن هذا المعنى قوله: دعاءه إذ هو مصدر تشبيهي يقتضي وجوده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r6.claim: Another interpretation says people seek forbidden things as readily as permissible ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p19/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ويدع الإنسان في طلب المحرم كما يدعو في طلب المباح

FARRA:v1p91/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p91/r1.claim: Arabic can omit the plural wāw, relying on the preceding ḍamma; al-Farrāʾ cites سندع الزبانية, ويدع الإنسان and three poetic examples.
FARRA:v1p91/r1.anchor: وقد تسقط العرب الواو وهي واو جماع

FARRA:v1p91/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p91/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p91/r2.claim: The feminine yāʾ can likewise be omitted with the preceding kasra as its marker; ʿAntara’s line illustrates this in تكحلي وتخضب.
FARRA:v1p91/r2.anchor: يحذفون (ياء التأنيث) وهي دليل على الأنثى اكتفاء بالكسرة

BURHAN:v1p397/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p397/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p397/r1.claim: In spelling, one of two adjacent wāws is deleted for ease while the essential waw remains.
BURHAN:v1p397/r1.anchor: الثانى حذف الواو اكتفاء بالضمة قصدا للتخفيف فإذا اجتمع واوان والضم فتحذف الواو التى ليست عمدة وتبقى العمدة

BURHAN:v1p397/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p397/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p397/r2.claim: Waw is omitted in four verbs to signal an action’s speed and ease for its agent and the affected party’s ready response.
BURHAN:v1p397/r2.anchor: وقد سقطت من أربعة أفعال تنبيها على سرعة وقوع الفعل وسهولته على الفاعل وشدة قبول المنفعل المتأثر به فى الوجود

BURHAN:v1p397/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p397/r6.speaker: author
